extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism ontology from paper XML/PDF/OA figures; no unsupported figure digitization was fabricated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AamAP1-Lysine directly damaged or permeabilized the E. coli cytoplasmic membrane in the beta-galactosidase release assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure 3 is a graphical time course; exact release values were not tabulated locally, so only the direct-assay mechanism class and concentration set are retained.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AamAP1-Lysine directly retarded E. coli genomic DNA migration in a gel-retardation assay, with retardation starting at peptide/DNA ratio 1.9 and complete retardation at higher amounts.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports DNA binding potential but does not prove that DNA binding is the sole or primary killing mechanism in cells.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AamAP1-Lysine was modeled as more cationic and alpha-helical than the parent peptide after lysine substitutions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational and physicochemical modeling is not promoted to direct antimicrobial mechanism evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The discussion infers initial electrostatic interaction with bacterial surface components from cationic peptide chemistry and bacterial envelope composition.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No dedicated LPS-neutralization or teichoic-acid binding assay was present in the local material; this remains an inference, not a direct mechanism claim.
